title: What If GPS Ignored Einstein? You'd Be 10 Kilometers Off
subject: GPS satellite

scenes.text: What if GPS ignored Einstein? Your map would be wrong by miles within a day.
GPS satellites orbit about 20,200 kilometers up, moving roughly 14,000 kilometers an hour.
That speed slows their clocks by about 7 microseconds a day.
But weaker gravity up there speeds them up by about 45 microseconds.
Net result: satellite clocks run 38 microseconds fast every day compared with clocks on the ground.
Light travels about 11 kilometers in that time, so uncorrected, errors would pile up about 10 kilometers a day.
